basis: Best fit is haematologic for benign lymphoid/splenic organ neoplasms; umbrella includes thymic tumors and has no uniform infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Neurodevelopmental impairment predominates in clinically affected chromosome 21 aneuploidies; other organ abnormalities vary substantially across subtypes.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities and male infertility affect reproductive function; no endocrine or other axis involvement established.
Originally defined through developmental delay; phenotype remains uncertain and annotated neurodevelopmental delay occurs in only 5–29%.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and glucose dysregulation define disease; scoliosis and osteoporosis each reported in 1/3 (~33%), supporting skeletal involvement.
Malignant bone tumor arising in the clivus; no additional organ damage established as sufficiently common from supplied evidence.
Hearing loss and congenital lacrimal punctal abnormalities define syndrome; nasolacrimal obstruction is occasional (5–29%).
Definition specifically identifies erythroblastosis fetalis, an alloimmune red-cell disorder; listed children also include nonimmune neonatal anemia.
Organic acid metabolism disorder defined by encephalopathic crises, striatal injury and dystonia; swallowing difficulties reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Mast-cell-mediated inducible urticaria/angioedema affects skin and subcutis; laryngeal involvement is not established in at least 30%.
Benign tumor of the parotid salivary gland, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
CDK4-associated melanoma is a cutaneous melanocytic malignancy; genetic association alone adds no other organ.
Clonal malignant plasma-cell neoplasm defined by a solitary destructive bone lesion; systemic myeloma complications are outside this diagnosis.
Papillary tumor originates in urinary tract urothelium; bladder, renal pelvis and other urinary sites all map to renal.
Marrow failure defines syndrome; hypogonadism in 2/2 and Chiari I malformation in 1/2 support endocrine and neurologic involvement; evidence is a tiny series.
Patellar, neurodevelopmental and renal abnormalities define syndrome; laryngomalacia in 6/19 (~32%) supports pulmonary involvement; hair/dental findings omitted under cap.
Developmental delay/intellectual disability is common across major 17q duplication syndromes; skeletal and other organ findings depend on duplicated interval.
Intellectual disability and severe early retinal degeneration define syndrome and were present in all five reported patients.
Pressure-related central nervous system dysfunction defines syndrome; nausea and dizziness do not establish gastrointestinal or inner-ear damage.
Defective lymphocyte apoptosis causes chronic lymphoproliferation, splenic involvement and autoimmune cytopenias; hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury.
Neoplasm originates in the bronchi; endocrine tumor histology in a minority subtype does not establish endocrine disease across this umbrella.
Descriptive syndrome explicitly comprises congenital marrow fibrosis/pancytopenia, intellectual disability, neurologic abnormalities and ophthalmic abnormalities.
Primary immunodeficiency with abnormal lymphoid-cell proliferation; HLH and lymphoma are distinct complications, and documented fulminant hepatitis is below 30%.
Defined as injury of cervical sympathetic nerves; ear pain and vertigo do not establish ear damage, and underlying arthritis is a separate condition.
Autoinflammatory dermatitis and arthritis define disease; keratoconjunctivitis sicca in 9/22 (~41%) supports ocular involvement; GI symptoms lack established direct injury.
